I would change Ryan’s code from **SC to UA**, while urgently seeking a human review before the payroll run.

Ryan says he was not ill, so SC is inaccurate. His sister does not fall within the stated DEP definition, and BRV does not apply. Under the supplied coding rules, UA is therefore the applicable code. It does **not** mean he failed to call in: he rang Gary at 05:40 to say he could not attend, although the information given does not establish whether he explained the reason on that call.

I would add a factual note recording his call and his explanation to HR the following morning. I would also immediately email payroll, if contactable, the HR Manager and Gary, flagging that this second UA will automatically generate a termination letter. I would ask whether someone with authority can hold the letter or review the case urgently, including whether a statutory protection or an exception applies. I would not assume either applies.

The note and emails do not themselves stop payroll, and Gary is not expected to read email before noon. If nobody intervenes in time, the stated process means the letter will be generated and sent that day. I would not leave the known-incorrect SC code in place to prevent that outcome.
